Community benefits are an important consideration in SRP’s resource decisions, and this contribution reflects a shared focus on meeting local needs. Together, Valley Farms Energy Center and SRP are focused on meaningful ways to support Coolidge based on their priorities. “We value the collaboration with city leaders and SRP to support projects that provide meaningful benefits for Coolidge residents,” said Kyle Whittier, development director at NextEra Energy Resources. “We appreciate the work the Center does to serve the community, and we are happy this contribution can help the facility remain available during power outages and other times of need.” "SRP’s commitment to communities expands beyond its service territory, and we are proud to partner with Valley Farms Energy Center to support Coolidge and its residents,” said Chelsey Falk, SRP manager of community activation. “This donation reflects our ongoing investment in the community and our dedication to helping address local priorities.” About NextEra Energy Resources NextEra Energy Resources, LLC, together with its affiliated entities, (“NextEra Energy Resources”) is America’s largest energy infrastructure developer and builder. The company develops, builds and operates long-term contracted power generation, battery storage and electric and gas transmission. NextEra Energy Resources also delivers integrated electric, gas supply and technology solutions to utilities, load-serving entities and businesses across the United States. As of year-end 2025, the company had approximately 37,505 megawatts of net generating capacity in operation. NextEra Energy Resources is a subsidiary of Juno Beach, Florida-based NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE: NEE). For more information, visit www.NextEraEnergyResources.com About Salt River Project SRP is a community-based, not-for-profit public power utility and the largest electricity provider in the greater Phoenix metropolitan area, serving about 1.2 million customers. OSS expects additional opportunities in 2027 and 2028 to support this testing and simulation platform. Based on current program expectations, OSS anticipates potential additional orders on this program in 2027 and 2028. We believe it may be another example of the growing base of multi-year platform opportunities we are developing across our defense and commercial markets.” About One Stop SystemsOne Stop Systems, Inc. OSS solutions address the overall AI workflow, from high-speed data acquisition to deep learning, training and large-scale inference, and have delivered many industry firsts for industrial OEM and government customers. As one of the fastest growing segments of the multi-billion-dollar edge computing market, AI enabled solutions require-and OSS delivers-the highest level of performance in the most challenging environments without compromise. articles.summary: TL;DR Manual cash application stays accurate when data is clean. The problem is that B2B customers bury payment details in unstructured PDFs, emails, and thin ACH or wire references. As ACH and wire volume grows, remittance data often gets thinner. A payment may carry only a short memo while the PDF remittance arrives separately, or never arrives. That creates the automation paradox. The payoff is not mainly fewer human errors. It is shrinking the gap between cash landing and an invoice being posted. Measure the dollar value of payments applied within 24 hours, not only the transaction match rate. That captures the working-capital effect more directly than a match percentage. Many organizations still run little to no AR automation, which forces analysts to chase fragmented payment data across channels before they can close an invoice. Some businesses still get paid late, partly because posting lags payment arrival when remittance shows up separately and unstructured. AI-driven platforms built on OCR, NLP, and machine learning can reach high matching accuracy when remittance data is reasonably complete, though that number should be verified in a live demo. Top performers push customers toward structured formats like EDI. Laggards receive more PDFs and loose data that slow reconciliation. The Short Version Yes, automating accounts receivable for PDF and email payments is worth it. Manual cash application can be very accurate when remittance data is clean. The problem is timing: customers send payment details in formats your team cannot process at scale, so cash lands before the invoice can be closed.
articles.title: How to Automate AR Cash Application When Payments Arrive as PDFs and Emails
